puzzle.atoms.name: Atoms
puzzle.atoms.tagline: Bond every atom into one molecule
puzzle.atoms.rule.1: Each atom's number is exactly how many bond-ends it must carry.
puzzle.atoms.rule.2: Bonds run straight, horizontally or vertically, between two atoms.
puzzle.atoms.rule.3: At most two bonds may join the same pair. Bonds may never cross.
puzzle.atoms.rule.4: Every atom must end up connected into a single molecule.
puzzle.atoms.rule.5: Tap between two atoms to cycle none, one, two, and back to none.
puzzle.atoms.rule.6: Or drag from one atom towards another to bond them.
puzzle.atoms.tutorial.1.caption: Each atom's number is how many bonds it carries. This 3 has three: one to the left, one to the right and one below.
puzzle.atoms.tutorial.2.caption: Two atoms can share one bond or two, never more. Bonds run straight, never cross, and every atom must join one molecule.
puzzle.atoms.tutorial.3.caption: This 2 has only one neighbour, the 3 below, so both its bonds go there. Drag from the 2 down to the 3 to lay one, then tap the bond to make it a double.
puzzle.atoms.tutorial.3.retry: Drag from the glowing 2 down to the 3, then tap the bond.
puzzle.atoms.tutorial.3.done: Doubled. A full atom turns blue.
puzzle.atoms.tutorial.4.caption: Tap the glowing gap twice for a double bond: it fills both 2s and cuts them off from the rest of the molecule, so it can't be right. Tap once more to clear it.
puzzle.atoms.tutorial.4.retry: Tap the glowing gap: once, twice, then once more.
puzzle.atoms.tutorial.4.done: Cleared. A tap goes none, one, two, and back to none.
puzzle.atoms.tutorial.5.caption: So those two 2s share one bond at most, and the corner 2 needs two. At least one must go up to the 2 above. Tap the gap between them.
puzzle.atoms.tutorial.5.retry: Tap once in the glowing gap.
puzzle.atoms.tutorial.6.caption: Your turn: finish the molecule. Stuck? Hint shows you why.
puzzle.atoms.tutorial.6.done: Solved. That's all there is to it.
puzzle.cages.name: Cage Sudoku
puzzle.cages.tagline: Sudoku where dashed cages must add up
puzzle.cages.rule.1: Fill every square with a digit from 1 to 9, as in Sudoku: no repeat in a row, a column or a 3x3 box.
puzzle.cages.rule.2: The dashed outlines are cages. The digits in a cage add up to the small number in its corner, and a cage never repeats a digit.
puzzle.cages.rule.3: Tap a square, then tap a digit. Tap the digit again to clear it.
puzzle.cages.rule.4: Or pick the digit first: with no square selected, tap a digit, then every square it goes in. Tap the selected square to let go of it, and the digit again to finish.
puzzle.cages.rule.5: Tap the pencil to take notes: while it is lit, a digit is pencilled small in the square instead of placed.
puzzle.cages.rule.6: Clashing digits, and cages that are over their total or finished wrong, are shown in red.
puzzle.cages.rule.7: Every row, column and box adds up to 45. That can tell you what the cages leave out, or spill into.
puzzle.cages.keyboard.1: Arrows move, 1-9 place a digit (or a note in pencil mode), Backspace clears.
puzzle.cages.tutorial.1.caption: Fill the grid as in Sudoku. The dashed outlines are cages: a cage's digits add up to the small number in its corner, and never repeat.
puzzle.cages.tutorial.2.caption: This cage totals 11 and already holds a 7, and 11 take away 7 leaves 4. Tap the empty square, then 4 below.
puzzle.cages.tutorial.2.retry: Tap the glowing square, then the 4.
puzzle.cages.tutorial.3.caption: A digit that breaks a rule turns red. Put a 5 in the glowing square: 5 + 2 is only 7, not 11, and its column has a 5. Then tap 5 again to clear it.
puzzle.cages.tutorial.3.retry: Tap the glowing square, then the 5, then the 5 again.
puzzle.cages.tutorial.3.done: Cleared. Tapping the digit again takes it out.
puzzle.cages.tutorial.4.caption: Not sure of a digit? Tap the pencil, then a digit, to jot it small. 11 take away the 2 is 9: pencil a 9 here.
puzzle.cages.tutorial.4.retry: Tap the glowing pencil, then the 9.
puzzle.cages.tutorial.4.done: Penciled. Tap the pencil again to go back to placing digits.
puzzle.cages.tutorial.5.caption: Your turn: finish the board. Stuck? Hint shows you why, cage totals included. Bigger cages take a little more working out.
puzzle.cages.tutorial.5.done: Solved. That's all there is to it.
puzzle.chess.name: Mate
puzzle.chess.rule.1: You play the side shown at the bottom. Checkmate the opposing king in the number of moves shown.
puzzle.chess.rule.2: Tap a piece, then tap where it goes. Tap another of your pieces to change your mind.
puzzle.chess.rule.3: The opponent answers each move. A move that lets them escape mate is not refused: you will be told, and can Undo.
puzzle.chess.rule.4: Standard chess rules, including castling, en passant and promotion (you choose the piece).
puzzle.chess.rule.5: Any mate within the moves counts, not only the one the hint knows.
puzzle.chess.tutorial.1.caption: Mate in 1: you play White and checkmate Black's king on g8. Its own pawns on f7, g7 and h7 box it in, and your rook on a1 can reach the back rank.
puzzle.chess.tutorial.2.caption: Tap the rook on a1, then tap a8. Two taps make one move: the first picks the piece up, the second puts it down.
puzzle.chess.tutorial.2.retry: Tap the glowing rook, then a8.
puzzle.chess.tutorial.2.done: Ra8#. Check on the back rank, and the king's own pawns block every way out.
puzzle.chess.tutorial.3.caption: Mate in 2: you move, Black replies, then you mate. Rd7 looks strong. Play it to see: tap the rook on d1, then d7.
puzzle.chess.tutorial.3.retry: Tap the glowing rook, then d7.
puzzle.chess.tutorial.3.done: Kb8, and no mate is left. In a game, Hint calls that a mistake.
puzzle.chess.tutorial.4.caption: Back to the start. Black's king has a7, b7 and b8. The quiet move is the key: tap your king on a5, then b6, to guard a7 and b7.
puzzle.chess.tutorial.4.retry: Tap the glowing king, then b6.
puzzle.chess.tutorial.4.done: Kb6. Black's one legal move was Kb8.
puzzle.chess.tutorial.5.caption: Now tap the rook on d1, then d8. Your king guards a7, b7 and c7, and the rook takes a8 and c8.
puzzle.chess.tutorial.5.retry: Tap the glowing rook, then d8.
puzzle.chess.tutorial.5.done: Rd8#. Every square the king could use is covered.
puzzle.chess.tutorial.6.caption: A pawn reaching the last rank becomes a piece. Tap h7, tap h8, then pick the queen: a rook would let the king escape to g7.
puzzle.chess.tutorial.6.retry: Tap the glowing pawn, then h8, then the queen.
puzzle.chess.tutorial.6.done: h8=Q#. The queen covers g7 and the h-file; your king covers g5 and g6.
puzzle.chess.tutorial.7.caption: Your turn: mate in 2. Stuck? Hint shows you why.
puzzle.cipher.name: Cipher
puzzle.cipher.tagline: Each letter is a digit. Make the sum true.
puzzle.cipher.rule.1: Each letter stands for one digit, 0 to 9, the same digit everywhere it appears.
puzzle.cipher.rule.2: Different letters are different digits, and no word starts with 0.
puzzle.cipher.rule.3: Give every letter its digit so the sum is true. There is exactly one way.
puzzle.cipher.rule.4: Tap a letter, then a digit. Tap the digit again to clear it.
puzzle.cipher.rule.5: Two letters on one digit, a word starting with 0, or a column that doesn't add up turns red.
puzzle.cipher.keyboard.1: Type a letter to pick it (H too, when the sum has an H), then a digit. Backspace clears, arrows walk the letters.
puzzle.cipher.tutorial.1.caption: Each letter is a digit, the same one wherever it appears, and no two letters share one. Find them so the sum is true.
puzzle.cipher.tutorial.2.caption: OUT is longer than TO and GO, so its O is what the tens column carries. Two digits and a carry make at most 19, so O is 1. Tap an O, then 1 below.
puzzle.cipher.tutorial.2.retry: Tap a glowing O, then the 1.
puzzle.cipher.tutorial.3.caption: The units column: O + O is 1 + 1, which makes 2, so T is 2. Tap a T, then 2.
puzzle.cipher.tutorial.3.retry: Tap a glowing T, then the 2.
puzzle.cipher.tutorial.4.caption: A digit that breaks a rule turns red. Give U the 1 that O already has: tap a U, then 1. Then tap 1 again to clear it.
puzzle.cipher.tutorial.4.retry: Tap a glowing U, then the 1, then the 1 again.
puzzle.cipher.tutorial.4.done: Cleared. Tapping the digit again takes it out.
puzzle.cipher.tutorial.5.caption: Your turn: finish the sum. Stuck? Hint shows you why.
puzzle.codeword.name: Codeword
puzzle.codeword.tagline: Each number is a letter. Crack the grid.
puzzle.codeword.rule.1: Every number stands for one letter, the same letter wherever it appears. Different numbers are different letters.
puzzle.codeword.rule.2: Every word across and down is a real word.
puzzle.codeword.rule.3: A few letters are given. Find the rest: there is exactly one way.
puzzle.codeword.rule.4: Tap a square or a number, then a letter. Tap the letter again to clear it.
puzzle.codeword.rule.5: A word that no word can match any more, or a letter on two numbers, turns red.
puzzle.codeword.keyboard.1: With a number picked, type its letter (again to clear it); Backspace clears, arrows walk the numbers.
puzzle.codeword.tutorial.1.caption: Each number is a letter, the same one everywhere, and no two numbers share one. T and E are given. Every word across and down is a real word.
puzzle.codeword.tutorial.2.caption: The top word reads {a} T E. Only ATE fits, so {a} is A. Tap one of its squares, then A.
puzzle.codeword.tutorial.2.retry: Tap a glowing square, then the A.
puzzle.codeword.tutorial.3.caption: The middle row reads E {x} T {r} A. Only EXTRA fits, so {x} is X. Tap {x} in the key under the grid, then X.
puzzle.codeword.tutorial.3.retry: Tap the glowing {x}, then the X.
puzzle.codeword.tutorial.4.caption: A letter on two numbers turns red. Give {r} the X that {x} has: tap {r} in the key, then X. Then tap X again to clear it.
puzzle.codeword.tutorial.4.retry: Tap the glowing {r}, then the X, then the X again.
puzzle.codeword.tutorial.4.done: Cleared. Tapping the letter again takes it out.
puzzle.codeword.tutorial.5.caption: Your turn: crack the rest. Stuck? Hint shows you why.
puzzle.codeword.tutorial.5.done: Solved: ATE, PEAT, EXTRA, TEEN and NET.
puzzle.dominoes.name: Dominoes
puzzle.dominoes.tagline: Lay every domino so each region keeps its rule
puzzle.dominoes.rule.1: Lay every domino from the tray on two neighbouring squares, either way round.
puzzle.dominoes.rule.2: Each coloured region has a rule. A number is the total of its pips; < and > bound the total.
puzzle.dominoes.rule.3: = means every square of the region shows the same; a crossed-out = means no two match.
puzzle.dominoes.rule.4: Squares outside a region have no rule, and a domino may cross from one region into another.
puzzle.dominoes.rule.5: Drag a domino from the tray onto a square and on into its neighbour: the way you swipe is the way it lies. Or tap it (again to turn it round), then two neighbouring squares. Its first half goes on the first square.
puzzle.dominoes.rule.6: Tap a laid domino to lift it; double-tap or long-press it to turn it round. Every board has one answer, found without guessing.
puzzle.dominoes.keyboard.1: Arrows move, ] or Tab and [ pick a domino, F or Space turns it, Enter marks a square and lays it, Backspace lifts.
puzzle.dominoes.tutorial.1.caption: Lay every domino from the tray so each coloured region keeps its rule. The 12 region's pips add up to 12: 6 + 6.
puzzle.dominoes.tutorial.2.caption: Only two 6s make 12, so the double 6 goes there. Tap it in the tray, then tap the two glowing squares.
puzzle.dominoes.tutorial.2.retry: Tap the glowing double 6 in the tray, then the two glowing squares.
puzzle.dominoes.tutorial.2.done: Laid. A domino covers two neighbouring squares.
puzzle.dominoes.tutorial.3.caption: A one-square region shows its pips: this one needs a 2, the 5-2's 2. Tap the 5-2, then this square, then the one below.
puzzle.dominoes.tutorial.3.retry: Tap the glowing 5-2 in the tray, then the glowing square, then the one below.
puzzle.dominoes.tutorial.3.done: The 5 landed on the 2: the half shown first goes on the first square.
puzzle.dominoes.tutorial.4.caption: Turn it round where it lies: double-tap the 5-2, or long-press it.
puzzle.dominoes.tutorial.4.retry: Double-tap the glowing domino, or long-press it.
puzzle.dominoes.tutorial.4.done: Turned. In the tray, a second tap turns a domino before you lay it.
puzzle.dominoes.tutorial.5.caption: = wants its squares the same: only 1 is on both dominoes left, and < 2 takes the 0. Drag the 1-0 from the tray onto the = square, then on to the right.
puzzle.dominoes.tutorial.5.retry: Drag the glowing 1-0 onto the glowing = square, then on into the square to its right.
puzzle.dominoes.tutorial.5.done: Both = squares will show 1, and 0 is under 2.
puzzle.dominoes.tutorial.6.caption: Changed your mind? Tap a laid domino to lift it back to the tray. Lift the 5-2.
puzzle.dominoes.tutorial.6.done: Back in the tray, and in your hand to lay again.
puzzle.dominoes.tutorial.7.caption: Your turn: lay the last two. Stuck? Hint shows you why.
puzzle.dominoes.tutorial.7.done: Solved. Every board works out one domino at a time.
puzzle.dwindle.name: Dwindle
puzzle.dwindle.tagline: Find every word, and watch the letters go
puzzle.dwindle.rule.1: Spell words by swiping through touching tiles, across or up and down (never diagonally), or tap them in turn and press Enter.
puzzle.dwindle.rule.2: A word has three letters or more and uses a tile at most once. Tiles never fall or move.
puzzle.dwindle.rule.3: The dashes show the goal words' lengths. Find them all to finish.
puzzle.dwindle.rule.4: Each tile's number is how many goal words still run through it. At zero it vanishes.
puzzle.dwindle.rule.5: Each goal word has only one way on the board, and no order can leave you stuck. Other real words are bonus words: they use nothing up.
puzzle.dwindle.keyboard.1: Type a word from the tiles, Backspace deletes, Enter tries the word, Escape clears it.
puzzle.dwindle.tutorial.1.caption: The dashes are the words to find. Each tile's number is how many of them still run through it.
puzzle.dwindle.tutorial.2.caption: Swipe through touching tiles to spell a word, across or up and down. Swipe C, H, E, F, then let go.
puzzle.dwindle.tutorial.2.retry: Swipe through the glowing tiles in order: C, H, E, F.
puzzle.dwindle.tutorial.2.done: CHEF fills its dashes, and each of its tiles' numbers drops by one.
puzzle.dwindle.tutorial.3.caption: A real word off the list is a bonus word: counted, never needed, and it uses nothing up. Spell EAT.
puzzle.dwindle.tutorial.3.retry: Swipe through the glowing tiles in order: E, A, T.
puzzle.dwindle.tutorial.3.done: EAT is a bonus word. The numbers did not change.
puzzle.dwindle.tutorial.4.caption: A has one use left. This time tap C, A and T in turn, then press Enter.
puzzle.dwindle.tutorial.4.retry: Tap the glowing tiles in order: C, A, T. Then press Enter.
puzzle.dwindle.tutorial.4.done: CAT. A is used up, so it vanishes.
puzzle.dwindle.tutorial.5.caption: Your turn: find the last words. Stuck? Hint gives you a clue.
puzzle.hexwords.name: Hexwords
puzzle.hexwords.tagline: Spend the letters well: every word uses them up
puzzle.hexwords.rule.1: Drag through touching hexes to spell a word of three to seven letters, or tap them in turn and press Enter.
puzzle.hexwords.rule.2: A word's letters leave the board, so a big word can break up the words around it.
puzzle.hexwords.rule.3: Three letters score 3, four 5, five 8, six 12, seven 17. Reach the target to finish.
puzzle.hexwords.rule.4: A word may come again from other letters. Nothing is lost for trying: Undo puts a word back.
puzzle.hexwords.keyboard.1: Type a word that traces on the board, Tab tries another way to trace it, Enter takes it, Backspace deletes, Escape clears.
puzzle.hexwords.tutorial.1.caption: Spell words through touching hexes to reach the target, 16 here. Longer words score far more: 3, 5, 8, 12 and 17 for three to seven letters.
puzzle.hexwords.tutorial.2.caption: Drag through A, N, C, H, O, R without lifting, then let go.
puzzle.hexwords.tutorial.2.retry: Drag along the glowing hexes in order: A, N, C, H, O, R.
puzzle.hexwords.tutorial.2.done: ANCHOR scores 12, and its letters are gone.
puzzle.hexwords.tutorial.3.caption: 4 points to go, but D, I, C and E don't touch in a way that spells anything. The biggest word cost the target. Undo puts a word back.
puzzle.hexwords.tutorial.4.caption: Look before you take. Start over with DANCE: tap D, A, N, C, E in turn, then press Enter.
puzzle.hexwords.tutorial.4.retry: Tap the glowing hexes in order: D, A, N, C, E. Then press Enter.
puzzle.hexwords.tutorial.4.done: DANCE scores 8 and leaves a word behind it.
puzzle.hexwords.tutorial.5.caption: Your turn: find the last 8 points. Stuck? Hint shows you why.
puzzle.hexwords.tutorial.5.done: Solved. Every letter earned its place.
puzzle.inequality.name: Inequality
puzzle.inequality.tagline: Each digit once per line, signs point to the smaller
puzzle.inequality.rule.1: Fill every square with a digit from 1 to the size of the grid.
puzzle.inequality.rule.2: No digit may repeat in a row or a column.
puzzle.inequality.rule.3: A sign between two squares points at the smaller one: the narrow end is the smaller digit.
puzzle.inequality.rule.4: Tap a square, then tap a digit. Tap the digit again to clear it.
puzzle.inequality.rule.5: A repeat, or a sign that is false, is shown in red as you go.
puzzle.inequality.keyboard.1: Arrows move, 1-6 place a digit, Backspace clears.
puzzle.inequality.tutorial.1.caption: Fill the grid with 1 to 4 so no digit repeats in any row or column. The bold digits are given.
puzzle.inequality.tutorial.2.caption: A sign sits between two squares and points at the smaller one. This one says the left square is smaller than the right.
puzzle.inequality.tutorial.3.caption: These four squares hold only 1s and 2s, and rows and columns can't say which goes where. The sign can: the top-left one is smaller. Tap it, then 1 below.
puzzle.inequality.tutorial.3.retry: Tap the glowing square, then the 1.
puzzle.inequality.tutorial.3.done: The sign settled the rest of that corner.
puzzle.inequality.tutorial.4.caption: A digit that breaks a rule turns red. Put a 1 in the glowing square: column 3 already has one. Then tap 1 again to clear it.
puzzle.inequality.tutorial.4.retry: Tap the glowing square, then the 1, then the 1 again.
puzzle.inequality.tutorial.4.done: Cleared. Tapping the digit again takes it out.
puzzle.inequality.tutorial.5.caption: Your turn: finish the board. Stuck? Hint shows you why.
puzzle.inequality.tutorial.5.done: Solved. That's all there is to it.
puzzle.kings.name: Kings
puzzle.kings.tagline: One crown per row, column and colour
puzzle.kings.rule.1: Place exactly one king in every row, every column and every coloured region.
puzzle.kings.rule.2: No two kings may touch, not even diagonally.
puzzle.kings.rule.3: Tap a square to pencil it out, and tap it again to rub the mark away.
puzzle.kings.rule.4: Double-tap or long-press a square to crown a king there, or to take the crown back.
puzzle.kings.rule.5: Drag across a run of squares to mark them all in one sweep.
puzzle.kings.rule.6: Squares a king already rules out are crossed off for you.
puzzle.kings.keyboard.1: Arrows move, Space pencils a square out, K or Enter crowns it, Backspace empties it.
puzzle.kings.tutorial.1.caption: Every row, every column and every colour holds exactly one king. Here are one row, one column and {second}, each with its one king.
puzzle.kings.tutorial.2.caption: Kings can't touch, not even corner to corner. None of the eight squares around a king can hold another.
puzzle.kings.tutorial.3.caption: A king on the glowing square would share a row with one {second} square and touch the other, leaving {second} nowhere. Tap it to cross it out.
puzzle.kings.tutorial.3.done: Crossed out. That square can never hold a king.
puzzle.kings.tutorial.4.caption: {first_cap_} has only one square left, so its king must go there. Double-tap or long-press it to crown it.
puzzle.kings.tutorial.4.retry: Double-tap the glowing square (two quick taps), or press and hold it.
puzzle.kings.tutorial.4.done: Crowned. The board crosses off every square it rules out.
puzzle.kings.tutorial.5.caption: {second_cap_} sits entirely in column 3, so column 3's king is {second}. Drag down the glowing squares to cross them all out in one sweep.
puzzle.kings.tutorial.5.retry: Drag along all three glowing squares in one sweep.
puzzle.kings.tutorial.5.done: Swept: one drag marks a whole run.
puzzle.kings.tutorial.6.caption: Your turn: finish the board. Stuck? Hint shows you why.
puzzle.kings.tutorial.6.done: Solved. That's all there is to it.
puzzle.lamps.name: Lamps
puzzle.lamps.tagline: Light every square, no lamp seeing another
puzzle.lamps.rule.1: A lamp lights its own square and its whole row and column, up to a wall or the edge.
puzzle.lamps.rule.2: Light every white square. No lamp may light another lamp.
puzzle.lamps.rule.3: A number on a wall is how many lamps sit right beside it: above, below, left or right.
puzzle.lamps.rule.4: Tap a square for a cross (a note that no lamp goes there), tap again to clear it. Drag to lay crosses across squares. Double-tap or long-press for a lamp; tap a lamp to remove it.
puzzle.lamps.keyboard.1: Arrows move, L or Enter places a lamp, X or Space a cross, Backspace clears.
puzzle.lamps.tutorial.1.caption: A lamp lights its own square and its whole row and column, up to a wall. Light every white square, and never let one lamp light another.
puzzle.lamps.tutorial.2.caption: A number on a wall is how many lamps sit right beside it: above, below, left or right. This 2 has two.
puzzle.lamps.tutorial.3.caption: The 0 has no lamps beside it. Tap the glowing square below it to cross it out: a note that no lamp goes there.
puzzle.lamps.tutorial.3.done: Crossed out. No lamp can go there.
puzzle.lamps.tutorial.4.caption: Its squares to the left and right are the same. Drag across the 0 from one glowing square to the other to cross out both in one sweep.
puzzle.lamps.tutorial.4.retry: Drag across the 0, from one glowing square to the other.
puzzle.lamps.tutorial.4.done: Swept: one drag crosses out a whole run.
puzzle.lamps.tutorial.5.caption: The 2 in the corner has only two squares beside it, so both hold lamps. Double-tap or long-press each glowing square to place one.
puzzle.lamps.tutorial.5.retry: Double-tap the glowing square (two quick taps), or press and hold it.
puzzle.lamps.tutorial.5.done: Two lamps, and their light fills their rows and columns.
puzzle.lamps.tutorial.6.caption: Your turn: light every square. Stuck? Hint shows you why.
puzzle.lamps.tutorial.6.done: Solved. Every square lit, and no lamp sees another.
puzzle.words.name: Lexicon
puzzle.words.rule.1: A word is hidden. Type a real word and press Enter to guess it.
puzzle.words.rule.2: Green: the right letter in the right place.
puzzle.words.rule.3: Yellow: the letter is in the word, but somewhere else.
puzzle.words.rule.4: Grey: the word has no (more) of that letter.
puzzle.words.rule.5: A letter is marked only as many times as the word holds it, so a second E can be grey while the first is yellow.
puzzle.words.rule.6: The keys keep the best clue for each letter.
puzzle.words.rule.7: Four-letter words have more look-alikes than five.
puzzle.words.keyboard.1: Type letters, Backspace deletes, Enter submits.
puzzle.words.tutorial.1.caption: A word is hidden, here one of four letters. Every guess must be a real word, and each letter comes back marked. Green means right letter, right place.
puzzle.words.tutorial.2.caption: Yellow means the letter is in the word, but not there: T and A are in it. Grey means the word has none of it: P and E are out.
puzzle.words.tutorial.3.caption: Use what you know: T and A are in the word, so move them. BOAT puts them in new places. Type BOAT on the keyboard, then tap Enter to score it.
puzzle.words.tutorial.3.done: Scored: the word ends in OAT.
puzzle.words.tutorial.4.caption: COAT, GOAT or MOAT: guess them in turn and it could take three. CLOG can't be the word, but its C and G tell all three apart. Type CLOG and score it.
puzzle.words.tutorial.4.done: C is green and G grey: only COAT is left.
puzzle.words.tutorial.5.caption: Your turn: find the word. Stuck? Hint shows you why.
puzzle.words.tutorial.5.done: Found it. That's all there is to it.
puzzle.lits.name: LITS
puzzle.lits.rule.1: Shade exactly four squares in every region, forming an L, I, T or S tetromino.
puzzle.lits.rule.2: A 2x2 square of shading is never allowed.
puzzle.lits.rule.3: Two tetrominoes of the same letter may not touch edge to edge, even across regions.
puzzle.lits.rule.4: Tap a square to shade or clear it, or drag across several to do the same to each.
puzzle.lits.rule.5: A finished tetromino takes its letter's colour and carries the letter, so two blocks touching in one colour are the rule being broken.
puzzle.lits.rule.6: Squares that can no longer be shaded are crossed off for you.
puzzle.lits.keyboard.1: Arrows move, Space shades; Shift+arrow carries the shading along.
puzzle.lits.tutorial.1.caption: Shade four squares in every region so they make an L, I, T or S. The thick lines are the walls. Here's a finished board; the glowing T is one region's.
puzzle.lits.tutorial.2.caption: Two tetrominoes of the same letter may not touch along an edge, even across a wall. These two L's meet only at a corner, which is allowed.
puzzle.lits.tutorial.3.caption: The top region has exactly four squares, so its tetromino is the whole region. Drag through all four glowing squares to shade them.
puzzle.lits.tutorial.3.retry: Drag through all four glowing squares in one go.
puzzle.lits.tutorial.3.done: Shaded. A finished shape wears its letter.
puzzle.lits.tutorial.4.caption: Shading never fills a 2x2 square. Tap the glowing square to shade it: with the L it fills a 2x2. Then tap it again to clear it.
puzzle.lits.tutorial.4.retry: Tap the glowing square, then tap it again.
puzzle.lits.tutorial.4.done: Cleared. A drag that starts on a shaded square clears too.
puzzle.lits.tutorial.5.caption: Squares that can't be shaded any more are crossed off for you. The middle region has exactly four squares left, so drag through them.
puzzle.lits.tutorial.5.retry: Drag through the four glowing squares in one go.
puzzle.lits.tutorial.5.done: Another L, touching the first only at a corner.
puzzle.lits.tutorial.6.caption: On the left, the crossed squares would make an L touching the middle L, or fill a 2x2 with it. What's left is a T. Tap its bump to shade it.
puzzle.lits.tutorial.7.caption: Your turn: finish the board. Stuck? Hint shows you why.
puzzle.lits.tutorial.7.done: Solved. That's all there is to it.
puzzle.mambo.name: Sun & Moon
puzzle.mambo.tagline: Balance two symbols, never three alike in a line
puzzle.mambo.rule.1: Fill every square with a sun or a moon.
puzzle.mambo.rule.2: Each row and column holds equal numbers of suns and moons.
puzzle.mambo.rule.3: Never more than two of the same symbol side by side, in a row or column.
puzzle.mambo.rule.4: A = between two squares means they match; an x means they differ.
puzzle.mambo.rule.5: Tap a square to cycle moon, sun, empty.
puzzle.mambo.rule.6: Every puzzle can be solved by deduction alone.
puzzle.mambo.keyboard.1: Arrows move, Space cycles, M puts a moon, S a sun, Backspace clears.
puzzle.mambo.tutorial.1.caption: Fill every square with a sun or a moon. Each row and each column holds three of each, like the glowing row.
puzzle.mambo.tutorial.2.caption: Never more than two alike side by side. An = between two squares means they match; an x means they differ.
puzzle.mambo.tutorial.3.caption: Two suns sit together in column 3, so the square above them must be a moon, or there'd be three suns. Tap it once for a moon.
puzzle.mambo.tutorial.4.caption: The x says these two differ. The right one is a sun, so the glowing one is a moon. Tap it once.
puzzle.mambo.tutorial.5.caption: In row 4, the gap between two moons must be a sun. A tap goes moon, then sun, then empty: tap once and three moons ring red, then tap again for the sun.
puzzle.mambo.tutorial.5.retry: Tap the glowing square once, then once more.
puzzle.mambo.tutorial.5.done: A sun, and the red ring goes.
puzzle.mambo.tutorial.6.caption: Column 3 now has its three suns, so its last square must be a moon. Tap it once.
puzzle.mambo.tutorial.7.caption: Your turn: finish the board. Stuck? Hint shows you why.
puzzle.mambo.tutorial.7.done: Solved. That's all there is to it.
puzzle.mines.name: Mines
puzzle.mines.tagline: Every safe square, found without a guess
puzzle.mines.rule.1: Each number counts the mines in the squares touching it, corners included.
puzzle.mines.rule.2: Reveal every square without a mine. Reveal a mine and the board is lost: try it again from the start.
puzzle.mines.rule.3: Flag a square you are sure holds a mine. A flag is your note, never checked, and keeps its square from being revealed by mistake.
puzzle.mines.rule.4: A tap uses the tool under the board, Reveal or Flag; a long press uses the other. Every board can be cleared without a guess.
puzzle.mines.rule.5: Tap a number whose flags already match it to reveal all its other squares at once. A wrong flag there opens a mine and loses the board.
puzzle.mines.keyboard.1: Arrows move, Space or Enter reveals (on a number, reveals around it), F flags or unflags.
puzzle.mines.tutorial.1.caption: Each number counts the mines in the squares touching it, corners included. Reveal every square without one.
puzzle.mines.tutorial.2.caption: This 1 has only one hidden square beside it, so that square is a mine: reveal it and the board is lost. Flag it: long-press it, or choose Flag below and tap it.
puzzle.mines.tutorial.2.done: Flagged. A flag is your note: that square can't be revealed by mistake.
puzzle.mines.tutorial.3.caption: This 1 touches that mine, so its other hidden squares are safe. Tap each glowing square to reveal it.
puzzle.mines.tutorial.3.done: Safe. A number with all its mines found frees the rest.
puzzle.mines.tutorial.4.caption: This 1 has one hidden square left, so it is a mine too. Flag it.
puzzle.mines.tutorial.5.caption: This 1's mine is flagged, so its other squares are safe. Tap the 1 itself to reveal them all at once.
puzzle.mines.tutorial.5.done: All three at once. A wrong flag would open a mine here, so flag with care.
puzzle.mines.tutorial.6.caption: Your turn: reveal every safe square. Stuck? Hint shows you why.
puzzle.mines.tutorial.6.done: Cleared. That's all there is to it.
puzzle.mini.name: Crossword
puzzle.mini.tagline: A mini crossword. Solve the clues.
puzzle.mini.rule.1: Every row and column of white squares is a word, and each word has a clue: 1 Across, 2 Down and so on.
puzzle.mini.rule.2: Tap a square, then type. Tap it again to turn between Across and Down, or tap the clue.
puzzle.mini.rule.3: Letters cross: a letter in one word is a letter of the word across it.
puzzle.mini.rule.4: Once every square is filled, a word that is no word in the list turns red, and a note says if anything is still wrong. Each clue has exactly one answer.
puzzle.mini.keyboard.1: Type letters; Backspace clears. Arrows move (one the other way turns first), Space turns.
puzzle.mini.tutorial.1.caption: Every row and column of white squares is a word, and each has a clue. Letters cross: a letter of one word is a letter of the word across it.
puzzle.mini.tutorial.2.caption: 1 Across is "{clueA}": {acrossWord}. Tap the glowing square, then type {acrossWord}.
puzzle.mini.tutorial.2.retry: Tap the glowing square, then type {acrossWord}.
puzzle.mini.tutorial.2.done: {acrossWord} is in, and its first letter starts 1 Down.
puzzle.mini.tutorial.3.caption: 1 Down is "{clueD}": {downWord}. Tap the glowing square under the 1, tap it again to turn it Down, then type the rest.
puzzle.mini.tutorial.3.retry: Tap the glowing square twice, then type {downWord}.
puzzle.mini.tutorial.3.done: Tapping a square again turns it between Across and Down.
puzzle.mini.tutorial.4.caption: A slip is easy to mend. Tap the glowing square and type Z, then tap Del to clear it.
puzzle.mini.tutorial.4.retry: Tap the glowing square, type Z, then tap Del.
puzzle.mini.tutorial.4.done: Cleared. Del takes back the letter under the cursor.
puzzle.mini.tutorial.5.caption: Your turn: fill the rest. Stuck? Hint shows you why.
puzzle.mosaic.name: Mosaic
puzzle.mosaic.tagline: Flood the board down to one colour
puzzle.mosaic.rule.1: Squares of one colour joined edge to edge form a single area, drawn with a heavy outline.
puzzle.mosaic.rule.2: Pick a colour below, then tap an area to flood it with that colour.
puzzle.mosaic.rule.3: A flooded area merges with every neighbouring area already in that colour — growing one big blob is how you cover ground quickly.
puzzle.mosaic.rule.4: Turn the whole board one colour before the fills run out.
puzzle.mosaic.rule.5: The limit is the fewest fills the board can be done in, so every fill has to count.
puzzle.mosaic.rule.6: Tapping an area in its own colour does nothing and costs nothing.
puzzle.mosaic.keyboard.1: Number keys pick a colour, arrows move, Space or Enter pours it.
puzzle.mosaic.tutorial.1.caption: Touching squares of one colour make an area, outlined in black. Turn the whole board one colour. The line above counts your fills against the fewest this board needs: here 3.
puzzle.mosaic.tutorial.2.caption: Pick amber below, then tap the glowing violet area. It joins every amber area it touches: three at once, more than any other fill can.
puzzle.mosaic.tutorial.2.retry: Pick amber below, then tap the glowing area.
puzzle.mosaic.tutorial.2.done: Four areas became one. The bigger it grows, the more each fill takes.
puzzle.mosaic.tutorial.3.caption: 2 fills left, 3 colours. A fill wipes out a colour only by covering its last patch, so both fills must. Amber is down to one patch: pour teal into it.
puzzle.mosaic.tutorial.3.retry: Pick teal below, then tap the glowing area.
puzzle.mosaic.tutorial.3.done: Amber is gone. Two colours, one fill.
puzzle.mosaic.tutorial.4.caption: Every other area touches the teal one, and they're all violet. Pour violet into teal to finish.
puzzle.mosaic.tutorial.4.retry: Pick violet below, then tap the glowing area.
puzzle.mosaic.tutorial.4.done: One colour, three fills: the least it could take.
puzzle.mosaic.tutorial.5.caption: Your turn: one colour in 4 fills, none spare. Stuck, or out of fills? Hint shows you why.
puzzle.mosaic.tutorial.5.done: Solved. That's all there is to it.
puzzle.nonogram.name: Nonogram
puzzle.nonogram.rule.1: The numbers beside a row, or above a column, give the lengths of its runs of filled squares, in order.
puzzle.nonogram.rule.2: Two runs always have at least one empty square between them.
puzzle.nonogram.rule.3: Pick Fill or Cross under the board and tap squares. Drag along a row or column to sweep several at once.
puzzle.nonogram.rule.4: On a big board, pinch to zoom in. Zoomed in, a drag moves around the board instead of sweeping, and the corner button shows the whole board again.
puzzle.nonogram.rule.5: A cross just means "empty": it is a note to yourself and never counts against you.
puzzle.nonogram.rule.6: Solved when every row and column shows its numbers. Every board can be worked out one line at a time, with no guessing.
puzzle.nonogram.keyboard.1: Arrows move, F fills, X crosses, Space cycles, Backspace clears; Shift+arrow carries a mark along.
puzzle.nonogram.tutorial.1.caption: Each number is a run of filled squares in that row or column, in order. Row 1 reads "1 1": a single square, a gap, then another single square.
puzzle.nonogram.tutorial.2.caption: Rows 2 and 3 read 5, and the board is five squares wide, so every square in them is filled. Drag along each row to fill it in one sweep.
puzzle.nonogram.tutorial.2.retry: Drag along the whole glowing row in one sweep.
puzzle.nonogram.tutorial.2.done: Filled. A run as wide as its row has nowhere to move.
puzzle.nonogram.tutorial.3.caption: Row 4 reads 3 in five squares. Imagine a block of 3 pushed to the far left, then the far right: the middle square is covered both times, so it is filled. Tap it.
puzzle.nonogram.tutorial.3.done: Filled. A block pushed both ways shows which squares it cannot avoid.
puzzle.nonogram.tutorial.4.caption: Column 1 reads 2, and rows 2 and 3 already give it that 2, so the rest of the column is empty. Choose Cross under the board, then tap the bottom square.
puzzle.nonogram.tutorial.4.retry: Switch to Cross under the board, then tap the glowing square.
puzzle.nonogram.tutorial.4.done: Crossed. A cross is only a note that the square is empty.
puzzle.nonogram.tutorial.5.caption: Your turn: finish the picture. Stuck? Hint shows you why. On bigger boards, pinch to zoom in.
puzzle.nonogram.tutorial.5.done: Solved. Every board works out one line at a time.
puzzle.pearls.name: Pearls
puzzle.pearls.rule.1: Draw one closed loop through the middles of squares, moving up, down, left or right. It never crosses or branches.
puzzle.pearls.rule.2: The loop passes through every pearl. It need not visit every square.
puzzle.pearls.rule.3: On a black pearl the loop turns, and goes straight on through the next square on both sides.
puzzle.pearls.rule.4: On a white pearl the loop goes straight through, and turns on at least one of the squares just before or after it.
puzzle.pearls.rule.5: Drag through squares to draw; drag back along a line to rub it out. Tap between two squares to cross that edge out (a note).
puzzle.pearls.keyboard.1: Arrows move, Shift+arrow draws or rubs out the line that way, X then an arrow crosses that edge.
puzzle.pearls.tutorial.1.caption: Draw one loop through the middles of squares that passes every pearl. On a black pearl it turns; on a white pearl it goes straight.
puzzle.pearls.tutorial.2.caption: A black pearl turns, then runs straight on two squares each way. In the corner it can only go down and right: drag from two below it, through it, to two right of it.
puzzle.pearls.tutorial.2.retry: Drag along the glowing squares in one stroke, through the pearl.
puzzle.pearls.tutorial.2.done: Drawn. A black pearl's arms always run two squares straight.
puzzle.pearls.tutorial.3.caption: A white pearl goes straight through. This one sits on the bottom edge, so it can't go up and down: drag across it, from its left to its right.
puzzle.pearls.tutorial.3.retry: Drag along the glowing squares, straight through the white pearl.
puzzle.pearls.tutorial.3.done: Straight through. It turns at the corner just before it, as a white pearl must on one side.
puzzle.pearls.tutorial.4.caption: The square after a black pearl runs straight on, so no line leaves it sideways. Tap the glowing edge to cross it out.
puzzle.pearls.tutorial.4.retry: Tap once on the glowing edge, between the two squares.
puzzle.pearls.tutorial.4.done: Crossed. A cross is a note: no line here.
puzzle.pearls.tutorial.5.caption: What if the white pearl on the left turned? Drag from it one square right and see.
puzzle.pearls.tutorial.5.retry: Drag from the glowing white pearl one square right.
puzzle.pearls.tutorial.5.done: It can't: a white pearl goes straight, so it turns red.
puzzle.pearls.tutorial.6.caption: Drag back along that line, from the pearl's right to the pearl, to rub it out.
puzzle.pearls.tutorial.6.retry: Drag back along the red line, in one stroke.
puzzle.pearls.tutorial.6.done: Rubbed out. Dragging along a line takes it away.
puzzle.pearls.tutorial.7.caption: Your turn: finish the loop. Stuck? Hint shows you why.
puzzle.pipes.name: Pipes
puzzle.pipes.tagline: Rotate until every pipe joins up
puzzle.pipes.rule.1: Tap a tile to rotate it a quarter turn.
puzzle.pipes.rule.2: Water enters at the ringed tile; pipes joined back to it run full.
puzzle.pipes.rule.3: Finish with no loose ends: every pipe opening must meet another.
puzzle.pipes.rule.4: All the pipework must form one single connected network.
puzzle.pipes.keyboard.1: Arrows move, Space or R turns the tile.
puzzle.pipes.tutorial.1.caption: Each tile's pipes are fixed; only the way it faces can change. Turn the tiles until every pipe joins into one network, with no loose ends and no loops.
puzzle.pipes.tutorial.2.caption: Water comes in at the ringed tile and fills every pipe joined back to it. When the whole board runs full, it's solved.
puzzle.pipes.tutorial.3.caption: No pipe may point off the board: an edge straight runs along it, a corner bend faces in, a T's flat side faces out. A tap turns a tile clockwise. Tap each glowing tile.
puzzle.pipes.tutorial.3.done: Each fits the border the only way it can.
puzzle.pipes.tutorial.4.caption: The straight above now points down into this end, and every opening has to meet another. So this end must point up. Tap it.
puzzle.pipes.tutorial.4.done: Joined. A set tile tells you about the tiles beside it.
puzzle.pipes.tutorial.5.caption: Your turn: finish the board. Stuck? Hint shows you why.
puzzle.pipes.tutorial.5.done: Solved. That's all there is to it.
puzzle.pointers.name: Arrows
puzzle.pointers.tagline: Clear every arrow, without a bump
puzzle.pointers.rule.1: Tap an arrow and it slides off the board the way its head points, if nothing is in its way to the edge.
puzzle.pointers.rule.2: If another arrow is in the way, it bumps and you lose a life. Lose all three and the board is lost: try it again from the start.
puzzle.pointers.rule.3: Clear every arrow to win. Taking one away only ever opens the way for others, so look before you tap.
puzzle.pointers.keyboard.1: Arrow keys move between arrows; Enter or Space taps the outlined one.
puzzle.pointers.tutorial.1.caption: Every arrow slides off the board the way its head points, but only if nothing is in its way to the edge.
puzzle.pointers.tutorial.2.caption: The top arrow points left, and nothing lies between its head and the edge. Tap it.
puzzle.pointers.tutorial.2.retry: Tap the glowing arrow along the top.
puzzle.pointers.tutorial.2.done: Gone. A clear way out means it can always go.
puzzle.pointers.tutorial.3.caption: The arrow below points right, into the long one down the side. Tap it anyway, to see.
puzzle.pointers.tutorial.3.retry: Tap the glowing arrow in the second row.
puzzle.pointers.tutorial.3.done: Bump. That cost a life: lose all three and the board is lost.
puzzle.pointers.tutorial.4.caption: Clear what is in the way first: tap the side arrow, whose way down is clear, then the second-row arrow again.
puzzle.pointers.tutorial.4.done: Taking an arrow away only ever opens the way for others.
puzzle.pointers.tutorial.5.caption: Your turn: clear the last two. Which one is in the other's way?
puzzle.pointers.tutorial.5.done: Cleared. That's all there is to it.
puzzle.regions.name: Regions
puzzle.regions.tagline: Fill each region, equal digits never touch
puzzle.regions.rule.1: A region of N squares holds the digits 1 to N, each once.
puzzle.regions.rule.2: Equal digits may not touch, not even at a corner.
puzzle.regions.rule.3: Tap a square, then tap a digit. Tap the digit again to clear it.
puzzle.regions.rule.4: A repeat, or a touching pair, is shown in red as you go.
puzzle.regions.keyboard.1: Arrows move, 1-5 place a digit, Backspace clears.
puzzle.regions.tutorial.1.caption: Each region holds the digits from 1 up to its size, once each. These have four squares, so 1 to 4. Bold digits are given.
puzzle.regions.tutorial.2.caption: Equal digits may never touch, not even at a corner. This 3 rules out a 3 in every square around it.
puzzle.regions.tutorial.3.caption: This square touches a 2, a 3 and a 4, so none of those can go here, and its region needs 1 to 4. That leaves 1. Tap the square, then 1 below.
puzzle.regions.tutorial.3.retry: Tap the glowing square, then the 1.
puzzle.regions.tutorial.4.caption: A digit that breaks a rule turns red. Put a 1 in the glowing square: it touches the other 1. Then tap 1 again to clear it.
puzzle.regions.tutorial.4.retry: Tap the glowing square, then the 1, then the 1 again.
puzzle.regions.tutorial.4.done: Cleared. Tapping the digit again takes it out.
puzzle.regions.tutorial.5.caption: Your turn: finish the board. Stuck? Hint shows you why.
puzzle.regions.tutorial.5.done: Solved. That's all there is to it.
puzzle.sand.name: Sand
puzzle.sand.tagline: Pour every colour into a tube of its own
puzzle.sand.rule.1: Sort the sand: finish with every tube holding one colour, or nothing.
puzzle.sand.rule.2: Tap a tube to lift it, then tap another to pour into it. Tap the lifted tube again to put it down.
puzzle.sand.rule.3: A pour moves the colour on top, all of it or as much as fits, onto the same colour or into an empty tube.
puzzle.sand.rule.4: Every colour has its own symbol. There is no move limit, and Undo takes a pour back.
puzzle.sand.keyboard.1: Keys 1 to 9 and 0 pick tubes 1 to 10: the first lifts, the second pours. Escape puts the tube down.
puzzle.sand.tutorial.1.caption: Sort the sand so each tube holds one colour (each has a symbol too). A pour moves the top colour, as much as fits, onto the same colour or into an empty tube.
puzzle.sand.tutorial.2.caption: Tubes 1 and 2 both have cream on top. Tap tube 1 to lift it, then tap tube 2 to pour.
puzzle.sand.tutorial.2.retry: Tap the glowing tube 1, then tube 2.
puzzle.sand.tutorial.2.done: The cream went onto the cream.
puzzle.sand.tutorial.3.caption: Tube 3's two brown sit on a cream. Pour them into the empty tube 5, then pour tube 2's two cream onto tube 3.
puzzle.sand.tutorial.3.retry: Tap the glowing tubes, the one to pour from first.
puzzle.sand.tutorial.4.caption: Your turn: sort the rest. Stuck? Hint shows you why.
puzzle.sand.tutorial.4.done: Sorted. That's all there is to it.
puzzle.sets.name: Sets
puzzle.sets.tagline: All alike or all different, four ways
puzzle.sets.rule.1: Find sets of three cards where each trait is all the same or all different.
puzzle.sets.rule.2: The four traits are count, shape, shading and colour. Two alike and one odd, on any trait, is not a set.
puzzle.sets.rule.3: Tap three cards to claim a set. Find them all to finish.
puzzle.sets.rule.4: Cards are never used up — a tinted card is one you have already used, and it is still in play.
puzzle.sets.rule.5: Sets you have claimed sit above the board; tap one to light up its three cards again.
puzzle.sets.keyboard.1: Arrows move, Space or Enter picks a card.
puzzle.sets.tutorial.1.caption: Every card has four traits: shape (oval, diamond, rectangle), colour (amber, teal, violet), shading (solid, striped, outlined) and number (one, two or three).
puzzle.sets.tutorial.2.caption: Three cards are a set when each trait is all the same or all different. The glowing three are all ovals, and differ in colour, shading and number.
puzzle.sets.tutorial.3.caption: Two alike and one odd is not a set. Tap the three glowing cards to see.
puzzle.sets.tutorial.4.caption: Tap a card to pick it, and tap it again to let it go. Follow the glow: pick two cards, let one go, then pick another.
puzzle.sets.tutorial.4.done: Any two cards point to exactly one third.
puzzle.sets.tutorial.5.caption: {value1} Find it and tap it.
puzzle.sets.tutorial.5.done: A set! It moves to the strip above.
puzzle.sets.tutorial.6.caption: Your turn: one set left, and it uses a tinted card: cards are never used up. Stuck? Hint shows you why.
puzzle.sets.tutorial.6.done: Solved. That's all there is to it.
puzzle.shikaku.name: Shikaku
puzzle.shikaku.tagline: Cut the grid into numbered rectangles
puzzle.shikaku.rule.1: Divide the whole grid into rectangles.
puzzle.shikaku.rule.2: Every rectangle must contain exactly one number.
puzzle.shikaku.rule.3: That number is the rectangle's area in squares.
puzzle.shikaku.rule.4: Drag from one corner to another to draw a rectangle. Tap a rectangle to remove it.
puzzle.shikaku.tutorial.1.caption: Split the grid into rectangles. Each holds exactly one number, and that number is its area: this 6 covers six squares.
puzzle.shikaku.tutorial.2.caption: This 6 needs six squares, and any other shape would run off the grid or take in another number. Drag from one corner to the opposite corner to draw it.
puzzle.shikaku.tutorial.2.retry: Drag from one glowing corner to the opposite one.
puzzle.shikaku.tutorial.3.caption: Draw the 4 down the glowing squares: the right size, but then no number can reach the corner, and every square needs one. Then tap the 4 to remove it.
puzzle.shikaku.tutorial.3.retry: Drag along the glowing squares, then tap the rectangle once.
puzzle.shikaku.tutorial.3.done: Removed. A tap takes any rectangle away.
puzzle.shikaku.tutorial.4.caption: Only the 4 can reach the glowing corner, and just one of its rectangles covers it. Draw it. Then only one rectangle of the 3 reaches the square below: draw that too.
puzzle.shikaku.tutorial.4.retry: Draw the rectangle over the glowing square.
puzzle.shikaku.tutorial.4.done: Drawn: a square only one number reaches is that number's.
puzzle.shikaku.tutorial.5.caption: Every rectangle this 6 can make covers the square below it, so the other 6 can't use that square. That leaves the other 6 one rectangle. Draw it.
puzzle.shikaku.tutorial.5.retry: Draw the bottom 6's rectangle, clear of the glowing squares.
puzzle.shikaku.tutorial.6.caption: Your turn: finish the grid. Stuck? Hint shows you why.
puzzle.shikaku.tutorial.6.done: Solved. That's all there is to it.
puzzle.snap.name: Trail
puzzle.snap.tagline: One line, every square, numbers in order
puzzle.snap.rule.1: Draw one continuous line from 1 to the highest number.
puzzle.snap.rule.2: The line must pass through every square exactly once.
puzzle.snap.rule.3: It must reach the numbered squares in ascending order.
puzzle.snap.rule.4: Drag to draw. Lift off and carry on from the end whenever you like.
puzzle.snap.rule.5: Drag back along the line, or start again from a square on it, to rub it out.
puzzle.snap.tutorial.1.caption: Draw one line from 1 to the highest number. It passes through every square exactly once, and meets the numbers in order: 1, 2, 3, 4.
puzzle.snap.tutorial.2.caption: A corner touches only two squares. The line must come in by one and leave by the other, unless it ends there, and only the last number is an end.
puzzle.snap.tutorial.3.caption: Lines start on 1. Leave 1 any other way and this corner is left one way in: a dead end. Put your finger on 1 and drag into the corner.
puzzle.snap.tutorial.3.retry: Start on 1 and drag into the glowing corner.
puzzle.snap.tutorial.4.caption: Lift your finger whenever you like: the line stays. Put it back on the end of the line and drag down, the corner's only other way out.
puzzle.snap.tutorial.4.retry: From the end of the line, drag down one square.
puzzle.snap.tutorial.4.done: Carry on from the end any time.
puzzle.snap.tutorial.5.caption: The square to the right is 4, but 2 and 3 have to come first. So the line can only go down.
puzzle.snap.tutorial.5.retry: Drag down one square from the end of the line.
puzzle.snap.tutorial.5.done: Numbers come in order, never early.
puzzle.snap.tutorial.6.caption: Try dashing for 2: drag right two squares. The bottom corner is left one way in, a dead end, and the line must end on 4. Then start a drag on the glowing square to cut back.
puzzle.snap.tutorial.6.retry: Drag along the glowing squares, then cut back.
puzzle.snap.tutorial.7.caption: Take the corner now, while it still has two ways in. Leave it a pocket with one way in and the line can't finish. Drag into it.
puzzle.snap.tutorial.7.retry: Drag down into the corner from the end of the line.
puzzle.snap.tutorial.8.caption: Say you went for 3 first: drag right onto it. 2 has to come before it, so drag back one square along the line to rub that step out.
puzzle.snap.tutorial.8.retry: Drag onto the glowing 3, then back one square.
puzzle.snap.tutorial.8.done: Rubbed out. Only 2 is left to go to.
puzzle.snap.tutorial.9.caption: Your turn: finish the line. Every square once, 2 then 3, ending on 4. Watch for squares down to two ways in.
puzzle.sudoku.name: Sudoku
puzzle.sudoku.tagline: One to nine, once per row, column and box
puzzle.sudoku.rule.1: Fill every square with a digit from 1 to 9.
puzzle.sudoku.rule.2: No digit may repeat within a row, a column or a 3x3 box.
puzzle.sudoku.rule.3: Tap a square, then tap a digit. Tap the digit again to clear it.
puzzle.sudoku.rule.4: Or pick the digit first: with no square selected, tap a digit, then every square it goes in. Tap the selected square to let go of it, and the digit again to finish.
puzzle.sudoku.rule.5: Tap the pencil to take notes: while it is lit, a digit is pencilled small in the square instead of placed. Placing a digit clears it from the notes of the squares it sees.
puzzle.sudoku.rule.6: Clashing digits are shown in red as you go.
puzzle.sudoku.keyboard.1: Arrows move, 1-9 place a digit (or a note in pencil mode), Backspace clears.
puzzle.sudoku.tutorial.1.caption: Fill every row, column and 3x3 box with the digits 1 to 9, each once. The bold digits are given.
puzzle.sudoku.tutorial.2.caption: Row 1 has one empty square left, and it holds every digit but 6. Tap the square, then 6 below.
puzzle.sudoku.tutorial.2.retry: Tap the glowing square in row 1, then the 6.
puzzle.sudoku.tutorial.3.caption: A digit that breaks a rule turns red. Put a 9 in the glowing square: it shares a column and a box with a 9. Then tap 9 again to clear it.
puzzle.sudoku.tutorial.3.retry: Tap the glowing square, then the 9, then the 9 again.
puzzle.sudoku.tutorial.3.done: Cleared. Tapping the digit again takes it out.
puzzle.sudoku.tutorial.4.caption: Not sure of a digit? Tap the pencil, then a digit, to jot it small in the square instead of placing it. Pencil a 5 here.
puzzle.sudoku.tutorial.4.retry: Tap the glowing pencil, then the 5.
puzzle.sudoku.tutorial.4.done: Penciled. Tap the pencil again to go back to placing digits.
puzzle.sudoku.tutorial.5.caption: Your turn: finish the board. Stuck? Hint shows you why. Placing a digit clears the square's notes.
puzzle.sudoku.tutorial.5.done: Solved. That's all there is to it.
puzzle.tally.name: Tally
puzzle.tally.tagline: Keep the numbers that make every sum
puzzle.tally.rule.1: The number beside each row, and under each column, is its target.
puzzle.tally.rule.2: Remove numbers so that what is left in every row and every column adds up to its target.
puzzle.tally.rule.3: Pick Remove or Keep under the board and tap numbers. Drag along a row or column to sweep several at once.
puzzle.tally.rule.4: Keep circles a number you are sure of. It is only a note: a circled number counts exactly like any other left in.
puzzle.tally.rule.5: Solved when every row and column adds up. Every board has one answer, found without guessing.
puzzle.tally.keyboard.1: Arrows move, X removes, K circles, Space cycles, Backspace clears; Shift+arrow carries a mark along.
puzzle.tally.tutorial.1.caption: Each number on the edge is a target. Remove numbers until what is left in every row and column adds up to it: row 1 keeps 1 + 6 = 7.
puzzle.tally.tutorial.2.caption: Row 1 needs 7, and its 9 is bigger than 7 on its own, so the 9 can't stay. Tap it to remove it.
puzzle.tally.tutorial.2.retry: Tap the glowing 9 once, with Remove chosen under the board.
puzzle.tally.tutorial.2.done: Removed. A number bigger than what its line needs always goes.
puzzle.tally.tutorial.3.caption: Column 4 needs 3, so both of its 9s go. Drag down across the two of them to remove both in one sweep.
puzzle.tally.tutorial.3.retry: Drag along the glowing 9s in one sweep.
puzzle.tally.tutorial.3.done: Both gone. A sweep marks a run of squares along one row or column.
puzzle.tally.tutorial.4.caption: Row 2 now adds up to 10, 4 over its 6. Remove its 5 and see what happens.
puzzle.tally.tutorial.4.done: Too much: 4 + 1 can never make 6, so row 2 turns red, and column 2 with it.
puzzle.tally.tutorial.5.caption: So the 5 stays. Choose Keep under the board, then tap the 5 to circle it.
puzzle.tally.tutorial.5.retry: Choose Keep under the board, then tap the glowing 5.
puzzle.tally.tutorial.5.done: Circled: a note that you are sure. It counts like any number left in.
puzzle.tally.tutorial.6.caption: Your turn: make every row and column add up. Stuck? Hint shows you why.
puzzle.tally.tutorial.6.done: Solved. Every board works out one line at a time.
puzzle.target.name: Target
puzzle.target.rule.1: Reach the target. Pick two numbers and an operator, and the answer replaces them as a new tile.
puzzle.target.rule.2: Any tile equal to the target wins. Each number is used once, and you need not use them all.
puzzle.target.rule.3: Answers must be whole numbers from 1 to 9,999: no negatives, fractions or zero. Subtract and divide put the bigger tile first.
puzzle.target.rule.4: Tap a number, tap + − × ÷, then tap another number. Undo takes a step back.
puzzle.target.keyboard.1: Type a tile's number, then + - * /, then another tile's number and Enter. Backspace steps back.
puzzle.target.tutorial.1.caption: Reach 106 from these six numbers. Combine two with + − × ÷ and the answer is a new tile. It must be a whole number above zero: no 7 ÷ 2, no 5 − 5.
puzzle.target.tutorial.2.caption: 25 × 4 makes 100. Tap 25, tap ×, then tap 4.
puzzle.target.tutorial.2.done: 100 is a new tile, and 25 and 4 are used up.
puzzle.target.tutorial.3.caption: Your turn: make 106 from here. You need not use every number. Stuck? Hint shows you why.
puzzle.target.tutorial.3.done: Solved. That's all there is to it.
puzzle.tents.name: Tents
puzzle.tents.tagline: A tent beside every tree, none touching
puzzle.tents.rule.1: Put one tent beside every tree, up, down, left or right of it. Each tent belongs to one tree.
puzzle.tents.rule.2: Tents never touch each other, not even at a corner.
puzzle.tents.rule.3: The numbers say how many tents each row and column holds.
puzzle.tents.rule.4: Tap a square for grass (a note that a tent can't go there), tap again to clear it. Drag to lay grass across squares. Double-tap or long-press for a tent (grass sprouts around it); tap a tent to remove it.
puzzle.tents.keyboard.1: Arrows move, T or Enter places a tent, X, G or Space grass, Backspace clears.
puzzle.tents.tutorial.1.caption: Every tree gets one tent, right beside it: above, below, left or right. The number beside a row or column is how many tents it holds.
puzzle.tents.tutorial.2.caption: Tents never touch, not even corner to corner. None of the eight squares around a tent can hold another.
puzzle.tents.tutorial.3.caption: The glowing corner has no tree beside it, so no tent can go there. Tap it to mark it grass.
puzzle.tents.tutorial.3.done: Grass. That square can never hold a tent.
puzzle.tents.tutorial.4.caption: The top row needs two tents, and only two of its squares sit beside a tree, so both are tents. Double-tap or long-press each glowing square to place one.
puzzle.tents.tutorial.4.retry: Double-tap the glowing square (two quick taps), or press and hold it.
puzzle.tents.tutorial.4.done: Two tents, and grass sprouts around them.
puzzle.tents.tutorial.5.caption: The bottom row holds no tents. Drag along the glowing squares to mark them all grass in one sweep.
puzzle.tents.tutorial.5.retry: Drag along all five glowing squares in one sweep.
puzzle.tents.tutorial.5.done: Swept: one drag marks a whole run.
puzzle.tents.tutorial.6.caption: Your turn: finish the board. Stuck? Hint shows you why.
puzzle.tents.tutorial.6.done: Solved. That's all there is to it.
puzzle.tower.name: Codebreaker
puzzle.tower.rule.1: A secret row of coloured pegs is hidden at the top.
puzzle.tower.rule.2: Tap a colour to put it in the next empty slot, or tap a slot to put the chosen colour there. Submit a full row to score it.
puzzle.tower.rule.3: A filled pip means one peg is the right colour in the right slot.
puzzle.tower.rule.4: A hollow pip means one peg is the right colour in the wrong slot.
puzzle.tower.rule.5: Pips are not aligned with the pegs — working out which is which is the puzzle.
puzzle.tower.rule.6: Colours may repeat in the secret.
puzzle.tower.keyboard.1: Number keys fill the next peg with that colour, Backspace removes the last, Enter submits.
puzzle.tower.tutorial.1.caption: A code of three pegs is hidden. Each guess scores a filled pip per peg in the right colour and slot, and a hollow pip per right colour in the wrong slot.
puzzle.tower.tutorial.2.caption: Guess 1 was all teal and scored nothing, so teal isn't in the code. Guess 2 has two filled pips, but pips never say which pegs earned them.
puzzle.tower.tutorial.3.caption: Your row copies guess 2. Change only slot 1 and score it, and the new score tells you about that slot alone. Tap gold, then the glowing slot, then Submit.
puzzle.tower.tutorial.3.retry: Tap gold below first, then the glowing slot, then Submit.
puzzle.tower.tutorial.4.caption: Guesses 2 and 3 differ only in slot 1 and scored the same, so slot 1 is neither blue nor gold. Teal is out, so it's brown. Tap brown: it fills the first empty slot.
puzzle.tower.tutorial.5.caption: Your turn: finish the code and submit it. Stuck? Hint shows you why.
puzzle.tower.tutorial.5.done: Cracked. That's all there is to it.
puzzle.whoswho.name: Who's Who
puzzle.whoswho.tagline: Match everyone to everything from the clues
puzzle.whoswho.rule.1: Each row is a person and each column a category: their house, and one or two more. No two people share anything.
puzzle.whoswho.rule.2: The houses stand in a row, numbered from the left. Next to means one house either side; somewhere left of means a lower number.
puzzle.whoswho.rule.3: Tap a square, then an item under the board. With the tick chosen it is theirs; with the cross chosen it is not.
puzzle.whoswho.rule.4: A tick rules that item out of the rest of its column, and the square shows what is still possible.
puzzle.whoswho.rule.5: Tap a clue to strike it through once you have used it. It is only a note.
puzzle.whoswho.rule.6: Solved when every square has its tick and every clue is true. Every board has one answer, found without guessing.
puzzle.whoswho.keyboard.1: Arrows move between squares, 1-5 tick that item (Shift+1-5 crosses it), Backspace clears the square.
puzzle.whoswho.tutorial.1.caption: Each row is a person, each column a category. The clues fix one way to fill every square: Ann lives in house 2 and has the dog.
puzzle.whoswho.tutorial.2.caption: Clue 1 says Ann lives in house 2. Tap Ann's House square, then 2 under the board.
puzzle.whoswho.tutorial.2.retry: Tap the glowing square, then 2 with the tick chosen.
puzzle.whoswho.tutorial.2.done: Ticked. Nobody else can live in house 2 now.
puzzle.whoswho.tutorial.3.caption: Clue 1 is used up. Tap it to strike it through.
puzzle.whoswho.tutorial.3.done: Struck through: only a note, to keep your place.
puzzle.whoswho.tutorial.4.caption: Clue 2: Ben does not have the dog. Choose the cross under the board, then tap Ben's Pet square and the dog.
puzzle.whoswho.tutorial.4.retry: Choose the cross, then tap the glowing square and the dog.
puzzle.whoswho.tutorial.4.done: Crossed off. Ben's square no longer offers the dog.
puzzle.whoswho.tutorial.5.caption: Clue 4: Ben does not live in house 3. Cross 3 off in Ben's House square.
puzzle.whoswho.tutorial.5.retry: Tap the glowing square, then 3 with the cross chosen.
puzzle.whoswho.tutorial.5.done: Crossed off. House 2 is Ann's, so Ben has only house 1 left.
puzzle.whoswho.tutorial.6.caption: Only 1 is left in Ben's House square. Choose the tick and tick it.
puzzle.whoswho.tutorial.6.retry: Choose the tick, then tap the glowing square and 1.
puzzle.whoswho.tutorial.6.done: Ticked. That leaves Cara only house 3.
puzzle.whoswho.tutorial.7.caption: See what a wrong tick does: tick the dog for Cara.
puzzle.whoswho.tutorial.7.retry: Tap Cara's glowing Pet square, then the dog, with the tick chosen.
puzzle.whoswho.tutorial.7.done: Clue 3 turns red: the cat owner must live in house 3, and only Cara can.
puzzle.whoswho.tutorial.8.caption: So Cara has the cat, not the dog. Tap the dog again to take the tick off.
puzzle.whoswho.tutorial.8.retry: Tap Cara's glowing Pet square, then the dog.
puzzle.whoswho.tutorial.8.done: Taken back. Every board has one answer, so every clue can be kept.
puzzle.whoswho.tutorial.9.caption: Your turn: fill in the rest. Stuck? Hint shows you why.
puzzle.whoswho.tutorial.9.done: Solved. Every board works out one clue at a time.
puzzle.wordwheel.name: Word Wheel
puzzle.wordwheel.tagline: Spell every word in the grid from the wheel
puzzle.wordwheel.rule.1: Spell words from the wheel by swiping across its letters, or tap them in turn and press Enter.
puzzle.wordwheel.rule.2: Each letter on the wheel is used at most once in a word, and no word is shorter than the grid's shortest.
puzzle.wordwheel.rule.3: A word the grid holds fills its slot. Fill every slot to finish.
puzzle.wordwheel.rule.4: Other real words count as bonus words. They are never needed.
puzzle.wordwheel.rule.5: Shuffle moves the letters round the wheel and changes nothing else.
puzzle.wordwheel.keyboard.1: Type letters from the wheel, Backspace deletes, Enter tries the word, Escape clears it.
puzzle.wordwheel.tutorial.1.caption: Spell words from the wheel's letters to fill the grid. Each slot holds one word, and the longest uses every letter on the wheel.
puzzle.wordwheel.tutorial.2.caption: Swipe across B, R, A, I and N without lifting, then let go.
puzzle.wordwheel.tutorial.2.retry: Swipe across the glowing letters in order: B, R, A, I, N.
puzzle.wordwheel.tutorial.3.caption: Crossing letters help: this four-letter slot has R third, and BARN is the only word the wheel spells like that. This time tap B, A, R and N, then press Enter.
puzzle.wordwheel.tutorial.3.retry: Tap the glowing letters in order: B, A, R, N. Then press Enter.
puzzle.wordwheel.tutorial.3.done: BARN. Swipe or tap, whichever you like.
puzzle.wordwheel.tutorial.4.caption: A real word the grid does not hold is a bonus word: counted, never needed. Spell BRAN.
puzzle.wordwheel.tutorial.4.retry: Spell the glowing letters: B, R, A, N.
puzzle.wordwheel.tutorial.5.caption: Your turn: fill the last slot. Stuck? Hint gives you its clue.
puzzle.wordwheel.tutorial.5.done: Solved. That's all there is to it.
puzzle.sudoku.tier.1: Each digit has one place left in a row, column or box
puzzle.sudoku.tier.2: Some squares need every other digit ruled out
puzzle.sudoku.tier.3: Needs a pair, a locked digit or a what-if
puzzle.cages.tier.1: Cages of 2 to 4 squares, some digits given
puzzle.cages.tier.2: Cages up to 5 squares, fewer digits given
puzzle.cages.tier.3: Cages up to 7 squares, no digits given
puzzle.target.tier.1: Three large numbers among the six
puzzle.target.tier.2: Two large numbers among the six
puzzle.target.tier.3: One large number, and the answer uses all six
puzzle.cipher.tier.1: Each digit follows from a column or two
puzzle.cipher.tier.2: Some digits need every column at once
puzzle.cipher.tier.3: Some digits need a what-if across two columns
puzzle.hexwords.tier.1: 19 hexes; biggest word first often gets there
puzzle.hexwords.tier.2: 29 hexes; biggest word first always falls short
puzzle.hexwords.tier.3: 44 hexes; looking one word ahead falls short too
puzzle.dwindle.tier.1: 4x4 tiles, 6 or 7 words, words up to 5 letters
puzzle.dwindle.tier.2: 5x5 tiles, 10 to 12 words, words up to 6 letters
puzzle.dwindle.tier.3: 6x6 tiles, 15 to 18 words, words up to 7 letters
puzzle.whoswho.tier.1: 4 people, 1 thing each, clues name the person
puzzle.whoswho.tier.2: 4 people, 2 things each, clues link things
puzzle.sudoku.tip.1: A digit with one place left in its box goes there.
puzzle.sudoku.tip.2: A square with only one candidate left is settled.
puzzle.sudoku.tip.3: A row with one empty square has its missing digit decided.
puzzle.sudoku.tip.4: Two squares sharing the same two candidates own those digits.
puzzle.sudoku.tip.5: A box digit confined to one row is out of that row elsewhere.
puzzle.kings.tip.1: A region with a single square left must hold its king.
puzzle.kings.tip.2: A king crosses off its eight neighbours.
puzzle.kings.tip.3: A region inside one row owns that row's king.
puzzle.kings.tip.4: If a king leaves a row or colour with no square, it is wrong.
puzzle.mambo.tip.1: A matching pair side by side: both ends are the other symbol.
puzzle.mambo.tip.2: Same symbol at both ends of a gap: the middle one differs.
puzzle.mambo.tip.3: A row with all its suns placed has only moons left.
puzzle.mambo.tip.4: An = or x links two squares: settle one and you settle both.
puzzle.pipes.tip.1: An opening that would leave the grid is never right.
puzzle.pipes.tip.2: One network only: a closed ring cut off from the rest is wrong.
puzzle.pipes.tip.3: Tiles beside ones already set often have a forced turn.
puzzle.shikaku.tip.1: A number with one rectangle that fits: draw it.
puzzle.shikaku.tip.2: A 1 is its own rectangle, so draw those first.
puzzle.shikaku.tip.3: Squares every rectangle of a number covers can be claimed now.
puzzle.shikaku.tip.4: A lonely square points to the one number that can reach it.
puzzle.mosaic.tip.1: A fill that merges with neighbours covers more ground.
puzzle.mosaic.tip.2: The fill limit is the minimum: seek the fill that swallows most.
puzzle.mosaic.tip.3: There is no spare fill, so a wasted one is not made up.
puzzle.sets.tip.1: Each trait is all alike or all different: never two and one.
puzzle.sets.tip.2: Any two cards fix the one third card that completes a set.
puzzle.sets.tip.3: Cards are never used up: one card can be in several sets.
puzzle.atoms.tip.1: An atom with one possible neighbour bonds only to it.
puzzle.atoms.tip.2: Bonds never cross, so a bond rules out the lines it cuts.
puzzle.atoms.tip.3: A cluster closed off from the other atoms is wrong.
puzzle.snap.tip.1: A square with one way in or out must be an end of the line.
puzzle.snap.tip.2: Work back from the highest number as well as from 1.
puzzle.snap.tip.3: Count the squares between two numbers to check a route.
puzzle.lits.tip.1: A full 2x2 block is never shaded: use it to rule squares out.
puzzle.lits.tip.2: If every shape a region can take shares a square, shade it.
puzzle.lits.tip.3: Same-letter tetrominoes may not touch, even across regions.
puzzle.tower.tip.1: Filled pip: right colour, right slot. Hollow: wrong slot.
puzzle.tower.tip.2: Change one peg per guess and the pips show what it did.
puzzle.tower.tip.3: Colours may repeat: count the pips before ruling one out.
puzzle.tower.tip.4: A guess that could be the answer beats one that cannot.
puzzle.words.tip.1: A green square fixes that letter in that place for good.
puzzle.words.tip.2: Yellow means the letter is in the word, just not there.
puzzle.words.tip.3: Open with common, different letters to learn the most.
puzzle.words.tip.4: A guess that could still be the word can win on the spot.
puzzle.nonogram.tip.1: If clues and gaps fill a line exactly, fill it completely.
puzzle.nonogram.tip.2: In a 10-square line, a 6 always fills the middle two squares.
puzzle.nonogram.tip.3: When a run is complete, cross the squares on each side.
puzzle.nonogram.tip.4: Crosses are only notes; they never count against you.
puzzle.chess.tip.1: Count the king's flight squares before anything else.
puzzle.chess.tip.2: A check is often the key; a quiet move can be too.
puzzle.chess.tip.3: Ask what every reply allows, not only what you threaten.
puzzle.chess.tip.4: A move that spoils the mate is allowed; Undo takes it back.
puzzle.inequality.tip.1: A sign's narrow end points at the smaller digit.
puzzle.inequality.tip.2: A square below a neighbour can never hold the top digit.
puzzle.inequality.tip.3: In a chain a < b < c, a is at most two below the top digit.
puzzle.inequality.tip.4: A row or column with one gap left names its digit.
puzzle.regions.tip.1: A square touching a 3 can never be a 3, even at a corner.
puzzle.regions.tip.2: A region of two squares holds a 1 and a 2, nothing else.
puzzle.regions.tip.3: If all but one square in a region touch a 4, the 4 goes there.
puzzle.regions.tip.4: Count what a square's region and its neighbours already hold.
puzzle.tents.tip.1: A square with no tree beside it can never hold a tent.
puzzle.tents.tip.2: A tent's eight neighbours are all grass.
puzzle.tents.tip.3: A tree with one free square beside it: a tent there.
puzzle.tents.tip.4: A row at zero is all grass.
puzzle.cages.tip.1: A cage of two totalling 3 can only be 1 and 2.
puzzle.cages.tip.2: A cage of two totalling 17 can only be 8 and 9.
puzzle.cages.tip.3: A cage of three totalling 24 can only be 7, 8 and 9.
puzzle.cages.tip.4: A cage never repeats a digit, even across a box edge.
puzzle.cages.tip.5: A row, column or box adds up to 45: use it to find a lone digit.
puzzle.target.tip.1: Work backwards: which two numbers could make the target?
puzzle.target.tip.2: Make a big product near the target, then add or subtract.
puzzle.target.tip.3: Dividing can shrink a large tile into a handy small one.
puzzle.target.tip.4: You never have to use every number.
puzzle.target.tip.5: Subtract or divide, and the bigger tile goes first for you.
puzzle.cipher.tip.1: A total longer than the addends starts with a carried 1.
puzzle.cipher.tip.2: Two digits and a carry make at most 19, so a carry is 0 or 1.
puzzle.cipher.tip.3: X + Y ending in X: Y is 0, or 9 with a carry coming in.
puzzle.cipher.tip.4: Work from the units: each column tells the next its carry.
puzzle.cipher.tip.5: No word starts with 0, so 0 hides in a word's later letters.
puzzle.codeword.tip.1: A number twice in one word is a double letter: EE, LL, OO, SS.
puzzle.codeword.tip.2: Short words have the fewest look-alikes once a letter is in.
puzzle.codeword.tip.3: Q is almost always followed by U.
puzzle.codeword.tip.4: A letter already used is greyed: no other number can have it.
puzzle.codeword.tip.5: Every square is in two words: a crossing checks both.
puzzle.mini.tip.1: Start with the shortest words: the fewest words fit them.
puzzle.mini.tip.2: A crossing letter cuts a word down to a handful.
puzzle.mini.tip.3: Every square is in two words: check a doubtful letter both ways.
puzzle.mini.tip.4: Tap a square twice to read the clue going the other way.
puzzle.mini.tip.5: Stuck on a clue? Fill its crossings first.
puzzle.hexwords.tip.1: A corner hex has few neighbours: use it before they go.
puzzle.hexwords.tip.2: One long word beats two short ones, unless it splits the rest.
puzzle.hexwords.tip.3: Before taking a big word, look at what it leaves stranded.
puzzle.hexwords.tip.4: A three-letter word can mop up a stranded edge.
puzzle.hexwords.tip.5: Undo costs nothing: try a word, look at the gap, put it back.
puzzle.dwindle.tip.1: One use left means one word still to come through that tile.
puzzle.dwindle.tip.2: Corners have few neighbours, so few words pass through them.
puzzle.dwindle.tip.3: Tiles never fall, so a letter's neighbours stay its neighbours.
puzzle.dwindle.tip.4: Each goal word can be spelled only one way on the full board.
puzzle.dwindle.tip.5: Bonus words use nothing up, so try them freely.
puzzle.wordwheel.tip.1: The longest slot always uses every letter on the wheel.
puzzle.wordwheel.tip.2: A crossing letter cuts a slot down to a handful of words.
puzzle.wordwheel.tip.3: Shuffle the wheel when a word will not come.
puzzle.wordwheel.tip.4: A bonus word rules that word out for every slot.
puzzle.wordwheel.tip.5: Plurals and -ED or -ING forms are never grid words.
puzzle.tally.tip.1: A number bigger than what its line still needs must go.
puzzle.tally.tip.2: If removing a number would leave too little, it stays.
puzzle.tally.tip.3: Circled numbers that already make the target: the rest go.
puzzle.tally.tip.4: List the ways a short line can make its target.
puzzle.sand.tip.1: Pour onto a matching colour before using an empty tube.
puzzle.sand.tip.2: An empty tube is your spare room: try to keep one free.
puzzle.sand.tip.3: Uncover a colour only when it has somewhere to go.
puzzle.sand.tip.4: A finished tube never needs touching again.
puzzle.pointers.tip.1: An arrow with an empty line to the edge can always go.
puzzle.pointers.tip.2: Clearing an arrow never blocks another: free stays free.
puzzle.pointers.tip.3: Follow a blocked arrow's line to find what to clear first.
puzzle.pointers.tip.4: An arrow on the edge pointing outwards is always free.
puzzle.mines.tip.1: A number with all its mines found: the rest around it are safe.
puzzle.mines.tip.2: Two numbers sharing squares: compare what each still needs.
puzzle.mines.tip.3: Near the end, count the mines left against the hidden squares.
puzzle.mines.tip.4: A flag keeps its square from being revealed by mistake.
puzzle.dominoes.tip.1: A square with one free neighbour must pair with it.
puzzle.dominoes.tip.2: A one-square region tells you that square's pips outright.
puzzle.dominoes.tip.3: The tray holds one of each domino: count what is left.
puzzle.dominoes.tip.4: A big total over two squares needs big halves on both.
puzzle.lamps.tip.1: A 4, or a 3 against the edge, fills every square beside it.
puzzle.lamps.tip.2: A square boxed in by walls has to light itself.
puzzle.lamps.tip.3: No lamp where it would light both of a 1's last two squares.
puzzle.lamps.tip.4: Crosses help: a crossed square can still be lit from afar.
puzzle.pearls.tip.1: A black pearl on the edge of the board runs two squares inward.
puzzle.pearls.tip.2: Three white pearls in a row can never share one straight line.
puzzle.pearls.tip.3: A square with only one way in is never on the loop.
puzzle.pearls.tip.4: Never join the two ends of a line unless it is the whole loop.
puzzle.whoswho.tip.1: A tick rules that item out for everyone else in its column.
puzzle.whoswho.tip.2: If the baker has the cat, whoever can't own it isn't the baker.
puzzle.whoswho.tip.3: Left of means the last house can't be the one on the left.
puzzle.whoswho.tip.4: Strike a clue once it can tell you nothing more.
